issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s deposit of rent and related amounts with the court hearing an eviction proceeding can substantially satisfy the first-hearing tender requirement when the funds are under that court’s control and available to the landlord.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground of unpaid rent.
The tenant deposited the rent and related amounts to the landlord’s credit in the same court that later heard the eviction proceeding.
At the first hearing, the landlord was informed that the deposit could be withdrawn.
The deposited funds were in the court’s custody and could be paid to the landlord at that hearing.
issues.conclusion: The tenant substantially complied with the tender requirement, so the eviction application could not succeed on the asserted failure to tender the arrears. The appeal was dismissed, and a remand to determine whether the landlord had earlier refused monthly tenders was unnecessary.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 13(2)(i) of the East Punjab Rent Restriction Act, 1949 gives a defaulting tenant a final opportunity to avoid eviction by paying or tendering the arrears, interest and costs at the first hearing. A deposit in the custody and control of the court hearing the eviction proceeding, available for payment to the landlord at that hearing, may substantially satisfy that requirement. The Court distinguished Shri Vidya Prachar Trust v. Pandit Basant Ram on the facts and found it unnecessary to reconsider that decision; the earlier Punjab High Court decisions discussed there did not govern the outcome.

rule.if: rent_arrears_eviction_proceeding and tenant_deposited_rent_and_related_amounts and deposit_held_by_eviction_court and funds_available_at_first_hearing and landlord_informed_of_withdrawal

predicates.rent_arrears_eviction_proceeding: A landlord sought eviction of a tenant on the ground of unpaid rent.
predicates.tenant_deposited_rent_and_related_amount: The tenant deposited the rent due and the related amounts required to address the arrears.
predicates.deposit_held_by_eviction_court: The tenant placed the deposit in the custody of the court hearing the eviction proceeding.
predicates.funds_available_at_first_hearing: The deposited funds could be paid to the landlord at the first hearing.
predicates.landlord_informed_of_withdrawal: The tenant informed the landlord at the first hearing that the deposited funds could be withdrawn.

issues.definition: When a tenant facing eviction for rent arrears deposits the rent and related amounts with the court hearing the case, the funds are available at the first hearing, and the landlord is informed of their availability, the first-hearing tender requirement is substantially satisfied.
